title: What a Real Aston Martin DB5 Costs Today

scenes.text: A new Aston Martin DB5 cost four thousand one hundred seventy-five pounds in nineteen sixty-three. Today, the Hagerty price guide shows six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars for a nineteen sixty-five car. A barn-find project once sold for five times its estimate. And a restored one cost four hundred thousand pounds to restore. What a real DB5 costs today depends on which sale you believe, and we show them all.
scenes.caption: WHAT A REAL ASTON MARTIN DB5 COSTS TODAY

scenes.text: Our sources are the Hagerty valuation page, RM Sotheby's, Bonhams reports from Classic and Sports Car and Supercars dot net, Top Gear, Auto123, Wikipedia, Old Cars Weekly and the Private Fleet blog, plus Census Bureau, Energy Information Administration and Kelley Blue Book figures. We show disagreements, and label our own arithmetic. Running costs are mostly not in our sources, and we say so.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: HAGERTY (APR 2025) · RM SOTHEBY'S · BONHAMS VIA CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR AND SUPERCARS.NET · TOP GEAR · AUTO123 · WIKIPEDIA · OLD CARS WEEKLY · PRIVATE FLEET · CENSUS · EIA · KBB · DISAGREEMENTS SHOWN

scenes.text: Start with the launch price. RM Sotheby's and 007 Travelers give four thousand one hundred seventy-five pounds. The Private Fleet blog gives the same figure for the hardtop and four thousand four hundred ninety pounds for the soft top. Auto123 says four thousand two hundred forty-eight. By our arithmetic, the soft top cost seven and a half percent more than the hardtop.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S + 007TRAVELERS: £4,175 · PRIVATE FLEET: £4,175 HARDTOP, £4,490 SOFT TOP · AUTO123: £4,248 · £4,490 ÷ £4,175 = +7.5% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: That soft-top premium was three hundred fifteen pounds, by our arithmetic. The Private Fleet blog calls the DB5 expensive for its time but gives no comparison price, and our sources give no average car price for nineteen sixty-three, so we cannot say how expensive in relative terms.
scenes.caption: £4,490 − £4,175 = £315 (+7.5%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · PRIVATE FLEET: 'EXPENSIVE FOR THE TIME' (NO COMPARISON PRICE) · 1963 AVERAGE CAR PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Hagerty valuation page, with a value graph from July twenty twenty-four to April twenty twenty-five, shows six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars for a nineteen sixty-five DB5, with a ten point two percent change. The page does not say which condition that figure is for. A common-questions section on the same page gives about eight hundred sixty thousand, six hundred sixty-seven dollars for a good-condition car of average spec.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY (APR 2025): $659,000, +10.2% (07/24 → APR 2025), CONDITION UNLABELLED · SAME PAGE: ~$860,667 FOR A 1965 DB5 'IN GOOD CONDITION WITH AVERAGE SPEC' (DOES NOT MATCH)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, those two Hagerty figures differ by two hundred one thousand, six hundred sixty-seven dollars, about thirty-one percent. The page does not explain the gap. It could be a difference of condition or of method; we cannot tell. So we use six hundred fifty-nine thousand as the lower marker and eight hundred sixty thousand as the upper marker for a good car.
scenes.caption: $860,667 − $659,000 = $201,667 → +30.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · EXPLANATION OF THE GAP: NOT ON THE PAGE

scenes.text: Top Gear wrote in September twenty twenty-one that a fully restored DB5 is worth about one million dollars. Auto123 wrote in December twenty eleven that a good used DB5 was close to two hundred fifty thousand. By our arithmetic, that is four times as much in nine years, though the two writers describe different conditions.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR (27 SEP 2021): FULLY RESTORED ≈ $1 M · AUTO123 (27 DEC 2011): GOOD USED ≈ $250,000 · 4× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT OUTLETS / CONDITIONS)

scenes.text: RM Sotheby's London offered a nineteen sixty-four DB5 in twenty twenty-two with an estimate of six hundred twenty-five to six hundred seventy-five thousand pounds, or eight hundred fifty to nine hundred thousand dollars. It was restored in twenty fifteen and sixteen, and is listed as not sold. So at that estimate, buyers did not meet the price, or the seller did not meet the bids.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LONDON 2022, LOT 146: ESTIMATE £625,000–675,000 ($850,000–900,000); NOT SOLD · RESTORED 2015–16 · BIDS / RESERVE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Bonhams' Bond Street sale in December twenty twenty-one sold a nineteen sixty-five DB5, restored to concours condition, for five hundred eighty-six thousand two hundred pounds, as the top lot, according to Supercars dot net. The article says it was found as a barn find about seven years earlier, and that the specialist restoration cost four hundred thousand pounds.
scenes.caption: SUPERCARS.NET (8 DEC 2021): 1965 DB5, CONCOURS CONDITION, £586,200, TOP LOT, BONHAMS BOND STREET SALE · BARN FIND ~7 YEARS EARLIER · RESTORATION £400,000 · ESTIMATE AND PROVENANCE: NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, five hundred eighty-six thousand two hundred pounds minus four hundred thousand leaves one hundred eighty-six thousand two hundred. That would be the implied value of the car before restoration, if the sale price covered only the restoration. The article does not say what the seller paid for the car, so we cannot compute a profit.
scenes.caption: £586,200 − £400,000 = £186,200 (OUR ARITHMETIC; IGNORES PURCHASE PRICE, FEES AND OTHER COSTS — PURCHASE PRICE NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: A project car tells a different story. Classic and Sports Car reported on a Bonhams marque sale on the twenty-first of May twenty eleven, where a DB5 that had been off the road for thirty-five years sold for two hundred eighty-two thousand pounds against an estimate of fifty to sixty thousand. Eleven phone bidders and five absentee bidders competed, plus about seven in the room.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR (24 MAY 2011): BONHAMS 21 MAY 2011 — DB5 OFF THE ROAD 35 YEARS SOLD £282,000 vs EST £50,000–60,000 · 11 PHONE + 5 ABSENTEE BIDDERS + ~7 IN THE ROOM

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that is 4.7 to 5.6 times the estimate. The magazine argued that the same money would buy a fully restored example from most top specialists, so buyers paid restored-car money for an unrestored car. That is the article's view, and we note it was written in twenty eleven, when restored DB5s cost less than they do today.
scenes.caption: £282,000 ÷ £60,000 = 4.7× · £282,000 ÷ £50,000 = 5.6× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ARTICLE'S VIEW: PROJECT PRICED LIKE A RESTORED CAR (2011) · 'RESTORED DB5s COST LESS THEN' = OUR INFERENCE FROM THE TOP GEAR AND HAGERTY FIGURES

scenes.text: From the same sale, a DB5 shooting brake sold for four hundred thirty thousand five hundred pounds against an estimate of two hundred fifty to three hundred thousand. In August twenty nineteen, RM Sotheby's sold a nineteen sixty-five shooting brake for one point seven six five million dollars. The two sales are in different currencies, so we do not compute a multiple.
scenes.caption: BONHAMS 2011: £430,500 vs EST £250,000–300,000 (1.4–1.7× EST, OUR ARITHMETIC) · RM SOTHEBY'S 2019: $1.765 M vs EST $1–1.4 M · EXCHANGE RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → NO CROSS-CURRENCY MULTIPLE

scenes.text: At the top of the market sit the film cars. A Goldfinger-era DB5 sold at RM Auctions in twenty ten for four point six million dollars, according to Wikipedia. NBC reported two point six million pounds, or four point one million dollars. In August twenty nineteen, RM Sotheby's sold the Thunderball promotional car for six million three hundred eighty-five thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 2010 $4.6 M · NBC: £2.6 M ($4.1 M) · OLD CARS WEEKLY (16 AUG 2019): $6,385,000, RM SOTHEBY'S MONTEREY · PRIVATE FLEET: £2.3 M (2010) — A THIRD FIGURE

scenes.text: The Private Fleet blog gives the twenty ten sale as two point three million pounds, a third number for the same event. It also says the car was used in Goldfinger and, it writes, Thunderbird, which is a slip for Thunderball. We treat the blog as the weakest of the three sources and show all of the figures.
scenes.caption: PRIVATE FLEET: £2.3 M (2010); WRITES 'THUNDERBIRD' FOR 'THUNDERBALL' · NBC: £2.6 M · WIKIPEDIA: $4.6 M → THREE DIFFERENT FIGURES FOR THE 2010 SALE

scenes.text: A stunt car from No Time to Die, one of eight replicas, sold for two point nine two million pounds at a twenty twenty-two charity auction, Wikipedia says. And the continuation cars, twenty-five Goldfinger-themed DB5s, were priced at about two point seven five million pounds, which CNN converts to three and a half million dollars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: NO TIME TO DIE STUNT CAR £2.92 M (2022 CHARITY AUCTION); 8 REPLICAS BUILT · CONTINUATION: 25 CARS, ~£2.75 M (WIKIPEDIA); CNN: ≈ $3.5 M

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, a film-linked car sold for between seven and ten times the Hagerty figure. The Bond provenance premium is huge, but only a handful of cars carry it. For an ordinary buyer, the relevant range is the first set of numbers: roughly five hundred to nine hundred thousand dollars, or one million for a perfect restoration.
scenes.caption: $4.6 M ÷ $659,000 = 7.0× · $6.385 M ÷ $659,000 = 9.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT YEARS; HAGERTY CONDITION UNLABELLED) · 'ORDINARY BUYER RANGE' = OUR SYNTHESIS OF HAGERTY, RM LONDON, TOP GEAR

scenes.text: Wikipedia mentions a nineteen sixty-five Vantage restored over three years and two thousand five hundred hours at a cost of four hundred thousand pounds. It was bought second-hand for nine hundred pounds in nineteen seventy-three and is estimated at one million pounds after restoration. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred sixty pounds for each hour of work.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1965 VANTAGE — 3 YEARS, 2,500 HOURS, £400,000; BOUGHT 1973 FOR £900; EST. £1 M AFTER · £400,000 ÷ 2,500 = £160/HR (OUR ARITHMETIC)
scenes.chapter: The cost to get one right

scenes.text: The Bonhams concours car also cost four hundred thousand pounds to restore, according to Supercars dot net. Two separate reports of the same figure suggest it is a typical order of magnitude, though they might be the same car, since we cannot tell. By our arithmetic, four hundred thousand pounds is ninety-six times the DB5's new price.
scenes.caption: SUPERCARS.NET: £400,000 RESTORATION (BONHAMS 2021 CAR) · WIKIPEDIA: £400,000 (VANTAGE) — SAME CAR OR NOT: NOT STATED · £400,000 ÷ £4,175 = 95.8× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Modern upgrades add more. RM Sotheby's lists a high-output alternator, LED headlamps, electronic ignition and a new twin-evaporator air-conditioning system added by Clayton Classics to its catalogue car. The catalogue gives no prices for those items. It also notes that an export licence is required if the car leaves the United Kingdom, a cost of time if not money.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LOT 146: CLAYTON CLASSICS — HIGH-OUTPUT ALTERNATOR, LED HEADLAMPS, ELECTRONIC IGNITION, TWIN-EVAPORATOR A/C · PRICES: NOT GIVEN · EXPORT LICENCE REQUIRED IF IT LEAVES THE UK

scenes.text: For the Thunderball car, Ecurie says Roos Engineering in Switzerland refurbished all thirteen of Adam's modifications. Roos is one of thirteen Aston Martin Heritage Specialists, it says. The cost of that restoration is not in our sources. So we can say a specialist exists, and that the film car was returned to working order, but not what it cost.
scenes.caption: ECURIE: ROOS ENGINEERING (SWITZERLAND), ONE OF 13 ASTON MARTIN HERITAGE SPECIALISTS, REFURBISHED ALL 13 ADAM MODIFICATIONS · COST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Running costs are largely missing. We searched for DB5 fuel economy and found no figure; a fuel-economy site we checked does not list the DB5, and gives only a brand-wide average of fourteen point eight miles per gallon, spanning cars from nineteen eighty-four to twenty twenty-seven. That average is not about the DB5, so we do not use it for the car.
scenes.caption: FORCAR.ORG: DB5 NOT LISTED; BRAND-WIDE AVERAGE 14.8 MPG (1984–2027 MODELS) — NOT APPLICABLE TO THE DB5 · DB5 MPG, TANK SIZE, SERVICE COSTS, INSURANCE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What we can say is what fuel costs. The Energy Information Administration put regular gasoline at four dollars twenty-eight cents a gallon for the week of the nineteenth of October twenty twenty-six. The DB5's premium fuel needs and consumption are not in our sources. Every ten dollars buys about two point three gallons at that price, by our arithmetic.
scenes.caption: EIA: REGULAR GASOLINE $4.284/GAL, WEEK OF 19 OCT 2026 · $10 ÷ $4.284 = 2.33 GAL (OUR ARITHMETIC) · DB5 FUEL REQUIREMENT / MPG: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Insurance appears only as marketing. The Hagerty page says it offers coverage built for classics, but gives no premium. We know from RM Sotheby's that some DB5s carry registration and export constraints. Beyond that, we do not have a source for storage, servicing or insurance costs. We will not invent a yearly figure, and you should be wary of anyone who gives one without a source.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY PAGE: 'COVERAGE BUILT FOR CLASSICS' — NO PREMIUM GIVEN · STORAGE / SERVICE / INSURANCE COSTS FOR A DB5: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → NO YEARLY FIGURE COMPUTED

scenes.text: Scale. Median U.S. household income was eighty-three thousand seven hundred thirty dollars in twenty twenty-four, says the Census Bureau. By our arithmetic, six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars is about seven point nine years of that income, and eight hundred sixty thousand is ten point three years. The average new vehicle was fifty thousand and eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six, per Kelley Blue Book.
scenes.caption: CENSUS 2024 MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $83,730 · $659,000 ÷ $83,730 = 7.9 YR; $860,667 ÷ $83,730 = 10.3 YR · KBB AVG NEW VEHICLE AUG 2026 $50,089 (OUR ARITHMETIC; GROSS INCOME)
scenes.chapter: Putting the price in human terms

scenes.text: So a DB5 at the Hagerty figure is about thirteen average new vehicles, and at the higher figure about seventeen, by our arithmetic. A new DB12, at two hundred forty-nine thousand dollars sticker according to Kelley Blue Book, is about five. In this comparison, a sixty-year-old DB5 costs more than two and a half new DB12 coupes.
scenes.caption: $659,000 ÷ $50,089 = 13.2 · $860,667 ÷ $50,089 = 17.2 · $249,000 ÷ $50,089 = 5.0 · $659,000 ÷ $249,000 = 2.65 (OUR ARITHMETIC; KBB DB12 MSRP $249,000)

scenes.text: Against the launch price, the arithmetic is more dramatic but less meaningful. Six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars is a different currency from four thousand one hundred seventy-five pounds, and our sources give no exchange rate or inflation index. The 007 Travelers page does record two hundred thousand pounds in two thousand six. By our arithmetic, that is forty-eight times the new price.
scenes.caption: 007TRAVELERS: £200,000 (2006) · £200,000 ÷ £4,175 = 47.9× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · EXCHANGE RATES AND INFLATION INDEX: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Hagerty page's ten point two percent rise over about nine months is worth a note. By our arithmetic, applied to the six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollar figure, that is about sixty thousand dollars of change. But the page does not say whether the rise reflects sales or the guide's own revisions, and it is one condition-unlabelled data point.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: +10.2% OVER THE 07/24–APR 2025 GRAPH · $659,000 − ($659,000 ÷ 1.102) = $61,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BASIS OF THE CHANGE (SALES OR GUIDE REVISION): NOT STATED

scenes.text: If you cannot afford the real car, the continuation is not the cheaper option. Wikipedia says the twenty-five Goldfinger-themed continuation cars were priced at about two point seven five million pounds each. CNN converts that to about three and a half million dollars. We use CNN's conversion because our sources give no exchange rate.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: CONTINUATION ~£2.75 M · CNN: ≈ $3.5 M (CNN'S OWN CONVERSION) · EXCHANGE RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Using CNN's own conversion of three and a half million dollars, the multiple against the Hagerty figure is five point three. The continuation cars use two hundred ninety brake horsepower, Wikipedia says, a little more than the original two hundred eighty-two. They are new builds, not restored originals, so they are priced for a different kind of buyer.
scenes.caption: CNN: £2.75 M ≈ $3.5 M · $3.5 M ÷ $659,000 = 5.3× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 290 BHP vs ORIGINAL 282 BHP (+2.8%, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Bonhams Aston Martin sale of the twenty-first of May twenty eleven is a useful snapshot. Classic and Sports Car reported a declared total of six million pounds, from forty-five lots, all but one of which sold. By our arithmetic, that is an average of about one hundred thirty-six thousand pounds for each of the forty-four cars that found a buyer, if the total covers sold lots only.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR (24 MAY 2011): BONHAMS 21 MAY 2011 — DECLARED TOTAL £6 M; 45 LOTS; ALL BUT ONE SOLD · £6 M ÷ 44 = £136,400 (OUR ARITHMETIC; ASSUMES THE TOTAL COVERS SOLD LOTS ONLY)
scenes.chapter: What a whole auction tells you

scenes.text: The same report lists a barn-find DB4 convertible with about sixty thousand miles that sold for three hundred nine thousand five hundred pounds against an estimate of eighty to one hundred forty thousand. By our arithmetic, that is 2.2 to 3.9 times the estimate. A restored DB4 Series Five Vantage convertible was the top lot at five hundred seven thousand five hundred pounds.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: 1963 DB4 CONVERTIBLE BARN FIND (~60,000 MI) £309,500 vs EST £80,000–140,000 (2.2–3.9×) · DB4 SERIES V VANTAGE CONVERTIBLE (RESTORED) £507,500, TOP LOT

scenes.text: Lower down, a nineteen sixty-eight DBS Vantage replica used in an on-screen Bond film sold for one hundred six thousand pounds against fifty to seventy thousand. A nineteen eighty-six Volante, similar to the car in The Living Daylights, sold for one hundred seventy-two thousand against seventy to one hundred thousand. A twenty-oh-nine Rapide sold for one hundred twelve thousand, with proceeds going to Japan's tsunami relief fund.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: 1968 DBS VANTAGE REPLICA (ON HER MAJESTY'S SECRET SERVICE) £106,000 vs EST £50–70k · 1986 VOLANTE (LIKE THE LIVING DAYLIGHTS CAR) £172,000 vs EST £70–100k · 2009 RAPIDE £112,000, PROCEEDS TO JAPAN TSUNAMI RELIEF

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the replica beat its estimate by 1.5 to 2.1 times and the Volante by 1.7 to 2.5 times. The article argued these results showed strong demand for Newport Pagnell-built Astons. That was twenty eleven. The Hagerty and Top Gear figures we have for twenty twenty-one and twenty twenty-five suggest prices rose further, though the sources do not link the two directly.
scenes.caption: £106,000 ÷ £70,000 = 1.5× TO ÷ £50,000 = 2.1× · £172,000 ÷ £100,000 = 1.7× TO ÷ £70,000 = 2.5× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ARTICLE: STRONG DEMAND FOR NEWPORT PAGNELL ASTONS · 'PRICES ROSE FURTHER' = OUR READING OF SEPARATE SOURCES

scenes.text: Which DB5 you buy matters. Wikipedia says 1,059 were built, of which one hundred twenty-three were convertibles, and sixty-five were Vantage coupes with the stronger engine. Nineteen of the convertibles were left-hand drive and twelve had the factory Vantage engine. Rarer variants tend to cost more, as the shooting brake results show.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1,059 BUILT · 123 CONVERTIBLES (19 LHD; 12 VANTAGE ENGINE) · 65 VANTAGE COUPÉS · 'RARER COSTS MORE' = OUR READING OF THE SHOOTING-BRAKE RESULTS
scenes.chapter: Specifications that affect what you pay

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, convertibles were twelve percent of production, Vantage coupes six percent, and the Bond cars under half of one percent. The Hagerty price guide does not say which variant its figure represents, so we cannot say how much of the spread between six hundred fifty-nine thousand and eight hundred sixty thousand is down to specification.
scenes.caption: 123 ÷ 1,059 = 11.6% · 65 ÷ 1,059 = 6.1% · 4 ÷ 1,059 = 0.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · VARIANT BEHIND THE HAGERTY FIGURE: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Specifications also differ between sources, which affects how buyers read a listing. The Private Fleet blog gives a power output of two hundred ten kilowatts, a weight of fifteen hundred kilograms and a zero to one hundred time of just over seven seconds. Wikipedia gives two hundred eighty-two brake horsepower, fifteen hundred two kilograms and zero to sixty in eight seconds.
scenes.caption: PRIVATE FLEET: 210 KW; 1,500 KG; 230 KM/H; 0–100 KM/H 'JUST OVER 7 S' · WIKIPEDIA: 282 BHP; 1,502 KG; 145 MPH; 0–60 MPH 8 S

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, two hundred ten kilowatts is two hundred eighty-two horsepower, so those two agree. The acceleration figures do not: just over seven seconds to one hundred kilometres per hour is faster than eight seconds to sixty miles per hour. For a buyer, the lesson is that old-car specifications should be treated as marketing claims until verified.
scenes.caption: 210 KW × 1.341 = 281.6 HP (OUR CONVERSION) → MATCHES 282 BHP · 0–100 KM/H 'JUST OVER 7 S' vs 0–60 MPH 8 S → CONFLICT · 'TREAT AS CLAIMS' = OUR EDITORIAL ADVICE

scenes.text: Let us build three routes to a DB5 from the numbers above. Route one: buy a good car at the Hagerty guide figure of six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars, up to eight hundred sixty thousand. Route two: buy a project and restore it. Route three: buy a Bond-linked car at auction. Each route has a very different risk, and our sources only give pieces of each.
scenes.caption: ROUTES: (1) BUY GOOD — HAGERTY $659,000–$860,667 · (2) PROJECT + RESTORATION — BONHAMS 2011 £282,000; RESTORATION £400,000 (SUPERCARS.NET / WIKIPEDIA) · (3) BOND-LINKED — $4.6 M TO $6.385 M

scenes.text: Route two, by our arithmetic. The project car of twenty eleven cost two hundred eighty-two thousand pounds, and a specialist restoration is reported at four hundred thousand. Together that is six hundred eighty-two thousand pounds, though the two figures come from different cars and ten years apart. It does not include fees, transport or the owner's own time.
scenes.caption: £282,000 + £400,000 = £682,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT CARS, 2011 PURCHASE + A 2021-ERA RESTORATION COST; EXCLUDES FEES, TRANSPORT, TAX)

scenes.text: Compare that with the Bonhams concours car of twenty twenty-one, which sold for five hundred eighty-six thousand two hundred pounds as a finished car. By our arithmetic, the sum of project and restoration in route two is about ninety-six thousand pounds higher than that finished car. This is a rough comparison, but it hints at why finished cars can look like good value.
scenes.caption: £682,000 − £586,200 = £95,800 (OUR ARITHMETIC; ROUGH — DIFFERENT CARS AND YEARS) · 'FINISHED CARS LOOK LIKE GOOD VALUE' = OUR INFERENCE

scenes.text: Route three is the film cars. A DB5 with Bond provenance sold for four point six million dollars in twenty ten and six point three eight five million in twenty nineteen. By our arithmetic, route three is seven to ten times route one at the Hagerty figure. It is not a route most people can take, since the sources say only three Bond-modified cars survive.
scenes.caption: $4.6 M ÷ $659,000 = 7.0× · $6.385 M ÷ $659,000 = 9.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · OLD CARS WEEKLY + CNN: ONE OF 3 SURVIVING BOND-MODIFIED DB5s

scenes.text: There is also a middle path: the GoldenEye car. InsideHook reported in June twenty eighteen that a DB5 used in GoldenEye was heading to Bonhams at Goodwood, with an expert projection of three to five million dollars. The same car sold in two thousand one for two hundred ten thousand six hundred dollars. We do not have the twenty eighteen result in our sources.
scenes.caption: INSIDEHOOK (15 JUN 2018): GOLDENEYE DB5 — BONHAMS GOODWOOD, EXPERT PROJECTION $3–5 M; SOLD 2001 FOR $210,600 · 2018 RESULT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the expert projection was fourteen to twenty-four times the two thousand one price. That is a rise over seventeen years, from two thousand one to two thousand eighteen, which works out at roughly seventeen to twenty percent a year, compounded, if the car had sold at the projection. It did not necessarily sell at it, so we call this a ceiling.
scenes.caption: $3 M ÷ $210,600 = 14.2× · $5 M ÷ $210,600 = 23.7× · 14.2^(1/17) = 1.169 (+16.9%/YR); 23.7^(1/17) = 1.205 (+20.5%/YR) (OUR ARITHMETIC; PROJECTION, NOT RESULT; FINAL PRICE NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: A caution on all of this. Prices in these sources come from different years, currencies and conditions. Hagerty's guide is updated quarterly, the Bonhams results are from two thousand eleven and twenty twenty-one, the film cars from twenty ten to twenty nineteen. We have lined them up for scale. A buyer would need a current valuation from a specialist, which we do not have.
scenes.caption: SOURCE DATES: HAGERTY APR 2025 · BONHAMS 2011 / 2021 · RM 2019 / 2022 · RM AUCTIONS 2010 · CURRENT SPECIALIST VALUATION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One last number. The Hagerty page calls its guide updated quarterly and offers value-change alerts. If the ten point two percent rise continued for another year, by our arithmetic the six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollar figure would become about seven hundred twenty-six thousand. That is not a forecast, only the arithmetic of a rate, which can go down as well as up.
scenes.caption: $659,000 × 1.102 = $726,200 (OUR ARITHMETIC; ILLUSTRATION ONLY — NOT A FORECAST) · HAGERTY: GUIDE UPDATED QUARTERLY; VALUE-CHANGE ALERTS OFFERED

scenes.text: There is also what you do not pay for. The DB5 has no entry in the fuel-economy tables we checked, no published warranty and, in our sources, no standard service schedule. A buyer relies on a specialist such as Roos Engineering or Clayton Classics, both named in our sources, and on the paperwork. Their rates, other than the reported one hundred sixty pounds an hour for one restoration, are not given.
scenes.caption: FORCAR.ORG: DB5 NOT LISTED · SPECIALISTS NAMED: ROOS ENGINEERING (ECURIE), CLAYTON CLASSICS (RM SOTHEBY'S) · SERVICE SCHEDULE / RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · £160/HR = ONE RESTORATION'S AVERAGE (OUR ARITHMETIC FROM WIKIPEDIA'S £400,000 ÷ 2,500 HR)

scenes.text: And an owner of a nineteen sixty-four car, like the RM Sotheby's catalogue example, might also face the question of where to keep it. The catalogue notes the car was shown at the twenty twenty-two London Concours, which suggests display, not daily use. Storage and insurance are the missing lines in this budget, and we leave them open rather than guess.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S LOT 146: SHOWN AT THE 2022 LONDON CONCOURS · 'SUGGESTS DISPLAY' = OUR INFERENCE · STORAGE / INSURANCE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What is missing. The condition of the Hagerty six hundred fifty-nine thousand dollar figure. Servicing, insurance and storage costs for a DB5. Its fuel consumption. The final price of the GoldenEye car. Why the Hagerty page shows two values. And the exchange rates we would need to compare across years. If you have primary documents, put them in the comments.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: CONDITION OF HAGERTY $659,000 · SERVICE / INSURANCE / STORAGE · DB5 MPG · REASON FOR TWO HAGERTY VALUES · EXCHANGE RATES AND INFLATION INDEX
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: So a real DB5 today costs somewhere between about five hundred thousand and nine hundred thousand dollars for a good one, about a million for a perfect one, and several million if Bond drove it. That is our reading of the sources, and the spread is the point. In the other videos we compare the DB5 with the DB12, reveal its secrets and tell the Bond story. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
